description.en: An ontology for representing cyber threats, vulnerabilities, industrial assets, and cross-domain relations in ICS security.

comment.undefined: The intended objective or target of a cyberattack on a ICS.
An industrial controller (e.g., PLC, DCS) that receives commands from the supervisory system and drives actuators. RTU is modelled as a subclass.
A technique defined in the ATT&CK Enterprise matrix.
An ATT&CK ICS asset representing a technology or system component relevant to industrial environments.
The consequence or operational impact caused by a cyberattack on a ICS.
A network switch that connects devices within the same network segment of a ICS environment.
A physical device in the control layer that executes commands from a controller (e.g., motor, valve, pump).
A software tool or malware used by threat actors as part of ATT&CK campaigns.
A Common Weakness Enumeration entry describing a type of software or hardware weakness.
A vulnerability entry from the China National Vulnerability Database.
A Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures entry identifying a publicly known cybersecurity vulnerability.
Abstract parent class for pairs associating a device or protocol with a specific firmware or software version.
The parent organization of a security team or threat actor.
The control layer of a ICS architecture, comprising controllers, actuators, HMIs, host computers, and related devices.
Root class for all MITRE ATT&CK framework concepts, including tactics, techniques, threat actors, campaigns, and mitigations.
A network gateway connecting different network segments within a ICS environment.
A pair associating a controller with a specific firmware version.
A high-level adversarial goal in the ATT&CK framework (e.g., Initial Access, Lateral Movement, Impact).
A technique defined in the ATT&CK ICS matrix.
A known security vulnerability in a software or hardware component.
A pair associating a communication protocol with a specific version.
A mitigation measure defined in the ATT&CK Mobile matrix.
A Remote Terminal Unit; a type of controller that monitors field devices and relays data to the supervisory system.
A technique defined in the ATT&CK Mobile matrix.
The manufacturer of a ICS device (e.g., Siemens, Schneider Electric, Rockwell Automation).
A pair associating a DAQ device with a specific firmware version.
A sub-category of a data source used to detect ATT&CK techniques.
The supervisory host computer in a ICS that issues high-level commands to controllers and hosts SCADA or HMI software.
The perception layer of a ICS architecture, comprising sensors and data acquisition devices that interact with the physical environment.
An individual, group, or organization that conducts malicious cyber operations against ICS environments.
An ATT&CK data source representing a system or artifact that can be used to detect adversary techniques.
A structured textual description of a CVE entry.
A coordinated set of malicious activities or attacks attributed to a threat actor over a period of time.
A pair associating a CVE entry with its CVSS scoring information.
A mitigation measure defined in the ATT&CK ICS matrix.
A pair associating an actuator with a specific firmware version.
A tactic defined in the ATT&CK Enterprise matrix.
A server providing computing, storage, or application services in the ICS network.
A tactic defined in the ATT&CK ICS matrix.
A pair associating an RTU with a specific firmware version.
A pair associating an HMI with a specific software version.
A defensive security team responsible for monitoring and protecting ICS environments.
An operating system running on ATT&CK-relevant infrastructure (e.g., Windows, Linux, VxWorks).
A pair associating a sensor with a specific firmware version.
A Human-Machine Interface providing operators with a graphical view of the industrial process and control capabilities.
A software or hardware weakness as defined in the CWE taxonomy.
The organization (e.g., MITRE, NVD) that assigned a CVE identifier.
A Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition system for real-time monitoring and control of industrial processes.
A software tool used in offensive or defensive cyber operations.
A URL reference associated with an ATT&CK entity.
The network layer of a ICS architecture, comprising routers, switches, gateways, and communication protocols.
A mitigation measure defined in the ATT&CK Enterprise matrix.
A tactic defined in the ATT&CK Mobile matrix.
A network router that forwards traffic between network segments in a ICS environment.
A Data Acquisition device that collects measurement data from sensors and transmits it to controllers or host computers.
A physical sensor in the perception layer that measures process variables and transmits data to DAQ devices or controllers.
A specific method or procedure used by an adversary to achieve a tactic.
The technical infrastructure used by threat actors to support their operations (e.g., C2 servers, botnets).
An industrial or network communication protocol used in ICS environments (e.g., Modbus, OPC UA, Profinet, DNP3).
The container record of a CVE entry holding structured vulnerability metadata.
Abstract parent class for ICS devices that actively initiate communication with controllers or RTUs (DAQ, HostComputer, RTU, Sensor).
An ATT&CK-defined mitigation measure that reduces the effectiveness of an adversary technique.
Relates an actuator to its firmware version pair.
Relates a controller to its firmware version pair.
The date on which a CVE was published.
Relates a technique to the data components that can be used to detect it.
The software version or hardware firmware version of a device or protocol.
The language code of a CVE description (e.g., en, zh).
The CVSS base score of a vulnerability (e.g., 7.5).
Relates an ATT&CK asset to another related asset.
Relates a device version pair to a CNVD vulnerability entry.
A controller drives an actuator to perform physical actions.
Relates a sensor to its firmware version pair.
A threat actor or campaign uses a specific software tool or malware.
The date on which a CVE was rejected.
A communicating entity (DAQ, HostComputer, RTU, or Sensor) communicates with a controller.
The textual content of a CVE description.
A threat actor or campaign employs a specific ATT&CK technique.
Relates a CVE to the organization that assigned it.
Relates an RTU to its firmware version pair.
The functional type of an actuator (e.g., motor, valve, pump).
Indicates that an HMI application is hosted on a host computer.
Relates a data source to one of its data components.
An ICS technique targets a ICS asset, control-layer device, or network component.
The ATT&CK identifier of an entity (e.g., T1234, TA0001, G0001).
A threat actor, campaign, technique, or tactic employs a specific tool.
The platform or operating environment applicable to an ATT&CK entity (e.g., Windows, Linux, ICS).
Relates a communication protocol to its version pair.
Relates a device version pair to a CVE vulnerability entry.
The name of the organization that assigned a CVE identifier.
A host computer communicates with a DAQ device.
Relates a CVE to the CWE weakness category it belongs to.
Textual description of an ATT&CK entity, used to support LLM-based entity alignment, graph fusion, and link prediction.
A security team is affiliated with a parent identity organization.
A sensor transmits measurement data to a DAQ device.
The CVSS vector string encoding the scoring metrics (e.g., CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/...).
A threat actor or campaign leverages technical infrastructure to support operations.
The CVSS base severity rating (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL).
A host computer or sensor communicates with an RTU.
Relates an HMI to its software version pair.
The date on which a CVE was last updated.
Relates a CVE entry to its structured description.
A threat actor initiates and conducts a campaign.
Relates a device version pair to a known vulnerability.
A URL or identifier referencing an external source related to an ATT&CK entity or CVE.
Relates a device or protocol to its firmware or software version pair.
A campaign or ICS technique causes an operational consequence on the ICS.
The name of the container record associated with a CVE entry.
Relates a technique to a recommended mitigation measure.
Relates a CVE to its container record holding structured metadata.
The intended objective or goal pursued by a campaign or threat actor.
Relates a DAQ device to its firmware version pair.
Relates a control-layer device to its manufacturer.
The title of a CVE entry.
An alias or alternative name used for a threat actor.
A tactic contains one or more techniques used to achieve it.
A ICS device supports a communication protocol.
A tool targets or operates on a software or system component.
